item.title: 美国宇航局阿耳忒弥斯二号机组人员荣获国会太空荣誉勋章
item.description:
从左到右：美国宇航局宇航员维克多·格洛弗和克里斯蒂娜·科赫、加拿大航天局宇航员杰里米·汉森和美国宇航局宇航员里德·怀斯曼于 2026 年 8 月 28 日从唐纳德·J·特朗普总统手中获得国会太空荣誉勋章，以表彰他们在阿耳忒弥斯二号任务中的贡献。
国会太空荣誉勋章于1969年由国会授权，以表彰在履行职责时因异常勇敢和功绩以及对国家和人类福祉做出贡献而表现出色的宇航员。自太空计划开始以来，目前已有 34 名获奖者获得该奖项，其中包括阿波罗 1 号、挑战者号和哥伦比亚号的机组人员，他们死后获得了该奖项。

item.title: NASA 在该机构 LunaRecycle 挑战第二阶段授予一等奖
item.description:
NASA 任命来自麻省理工学院 (MIT) 的一个团队为该机构 LunaRecycle 挑战第二阶段的一等奖获得者，该挑战的重点是开发解决方案，通过回收常见材料（如织物、塑料、泡沫和金属）来减少月球或深空任务期间的废物。
由麻省理工学院的本科生、研究生和博士生组成的 Zotek 设计再利用和升级再造外星回收复合材料 (CERBERUZ) 团队获得了总计 775,000 美元的奖项。
该技术将混合垃圾磨成细粉，重新利用 Zotek 泡沫等材料作为增强材料，而不是将其视为需要分类的污染物。粉末成为饲料，用作注塑成型零件或 3D 打印线材。麻省理工学院团队在竞赛的原型开发赛道和专注于开发回收系统虚拟模型（称为“数字双胞胎”）的赛道上均获胜。
“LunaRecycle 挑战赛的决赛是本次竞赛激发的两年创新的顶峰，”位于阿拉巴马州亨茨维尔的 NASA 马歇尔太空飞行中心百年挑战项目经理 Jennifer Edmunson 说道。 “在这段时间内看到这些技术从概念到原型和数字孪生演示真是令人难以置信。推动快速和创造性的创新正是 NASA 挑战的全部内容。”
LunaRecycle 是一项耗资 300 万美元、与阿拉巴马大学 Lee J. Styslinger Jr. 工程学院合作的两阶段竞赛。 竞赛的第二阶段要求美国团队提交一个原型，并可选用数字孪生作为其虚拟模型。
在第二阶段，来自美国各地的 14 支决赛团队于 8 月 24 日至 8 月 28 日聚集在塔斯卡卢萨的阿拉巴马大学 Lee J. Styslinger Jr. 工程学院，展示他们的技术原型。一些团队提交的数字孪生模型也与各自的原型一起展示。
参赛者的背景涵盖从大学生和教师到企业家和空间技术爱好者。 鼓励团队设想解决方案，不仅可以解决深空回收问题，而且还可以在地球上应用。
除一等奖获得者外，还有九支队伍获得了奖品：
“这场竞赛凸显了合作如何能够带来令人难以置信的解决方案，”负责管理 LunaRecycle 挑战赛的 Chris Frangione 说道，该挑战赛旨在支持通过 Amentum 太空探索部门签订的 NASA 百年挑战赛。 “在求解器团队、阿拉巴马大学和 NASA 之间，这个结局展示了当我们为了一个共同的目标汇集资源和伟大的想法时可以取得什么成就。”
第二阶段奖项是在第一阶段竞赛取得成功之后颁发的，第一阶段受到了全球创新者社区创纪录的关注，注册人数超过 1,200 人，超过了 NASA 百年挑战赛 20 年历史上的任何竞赛。 第一阶段将于 2025 年结束，来自世界各地的参与者可以在原型或数字孪生轨道中的一个或两个中提交设计。 由 50 名评委组成的评审团评估了近 200 份第一阶​​段提交的材料，选出代表 5 个国家和美国 9 个州的 17 支团队作为获胜者。 第二阶段的参赛作品必须与第一阶段无关。
LunaRecycle 挑战由 NASA 马歇尔太空飞行中心百年挑战赛管理，是 NASA 研究与技术任务理事会奖项、挑战和众包计划的一部分。 NASA 的百年挑战已有 20 多年的历史，它吸引公众解决复杂的问题，从而有利于 NASA 更广泛的计划。过去的挑战刺激了机器人、增材制造、电力和能源、纺织、化学和生物学领域的进步。
LunaRecycle 还得到了美国宇航局佛罗里达州肯尼迪航天中心、美国宇航局位于加利福尼亚硅谷的艾姆斯研究中心和美国宇航局位于弗吉尼亚州汉普顿的兰利研究中心的主题专家的支持。

item.title: 总统授予 NASA 阿尔忒弥斯二号机组人员美国最高太空奖
item.description:
President Donald J. Trump awarded NASA astronauts Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, and Christina Koch, and CSA (Canadian Space Agency) astronaut Jeremy Hansen with the Congressional Space Medal of Honor Friday for their service during the Artemis II mission. He presented the awards during a ceremony at NASA’s Johnson Space Center in Houston, honoring the first medal recipients since 2023.
NASA’s historic Artemis II mission launched on April 1, and splashed down safely in the Pacific Ocean on April 10. The crew members were the first astronauts to launch on the agency’s SLS (Space Launch System) rocket, flying aboard NASA’s Orion spacecraft, which the crew named Integrity. During theirrecord-setting mission, the astronauts traveled 252,756 miles from Earth, farther than any humans have traveled before, surpassing a previous record set by Apollo 13 astronauts in 1970. In total, they flew 695,081 miles, including a lunar flyby.
“We gather on these historic grounds to celebrate the immense courage of four intrepid space heroes whose sense of daring and adventure led them further from Earth than anyone has ever traveled ever before,” said President Trump. “Today we’re proudly awarding the Congressional Space Medal of Honor to the remarkable crew of Artemis II. These astronauts did not do it alone. I want to salute all of the engineers, and scientists, launch and landing specialists, everyone at NASA who helped make this mission a great success.”
The Congressional Space Medal of Honor was authorized by Congress in 1969 to recognize an astronaut who in the performance of duties has distinguished himself or herself by exceptionally brave and meritorious efforts, and contributions to the welfare of the nation and humanity. There now are 34 recipients of the award since the beginning of the space program, including the crews of Apollo 1, Challenger, and Columbia who received the award posthumously.
“President Trump’s leadership has put America back on a path to lead the world in space, from creating the Artemis program to giving NASA the resources and mandate to win this new space race,” said NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman. “The Artemis II crew answered that call with extraordinary skill and courage, showing the world the Moon again and what American leadership and exploration look like at their best. Their achievement was made possible by the exceptional NASA workforce, alongside our industry and international partners, who showed once again what can be accomplished when we commit to big, bold endeavors. We will build on this success as we return to the lunar surface and establish an enduring presence on the Moon.”
The first crewed mission under NASA’s Artemis program paved the way for the 2027Artemis IIItest flight in low Earth orbit to demonstrate rendezvous and docking capabilities between Orion and commercial human landing systems, and theArtemis IVmission in 2028, which will return American astronauts to the lunar surface.
“It was the honor of my lifetime to fly on Integrity around the Moon with Victor, Christina, and Jeremy. Having President Trump here at the agency’s Johnson Space Center to honor NASA and my crew underscores the significance of what our teams accomplished,” saidWiseman, who served as commander of the mission. “I can’t wait to see my friends continue this legacy on Artemis III.”
Glover served as pilot of the Orion spacecraft.
“Piloting Orion for the first time in space was a profound honor, made possible because of the years of hard work, dedication, and expertise by countless individuals dedicating their time and talents to the mission,” saidGlover. “We share this recognition with the thousands of people who launched us around the Moon and brought us safely back to Earth.”
“The response to our mission here on Earth was beyond anything we ever imagined and all we ever hoped for. We are grateful every time we hear from people who followed along with our journey. As team members on this shared mission, we accept this award to honor those who made it happen, from factory floors to clean rooms and mission control rooms,” saidKoch.
Hansen also served as a mission specialist.
“It is a privilege to receive the Congressional Space Medal of Honor alongside my Artemis II crewmates,” said Hansen. “I share this recognition with the dedicated teams in Canada, the United States, and our international partners who made the mission possible. Artemis II showed what we can accomplish for humanity when we set ambitious goals and work together. For Canada, the mission and the Artemis program as a whole are about much more than just going back to the Moon. It is about the pursuit of excellence and collaboration.”
As part of a Golden Age of innovation and exploration, NASA will send Artemis astronauts on a series of challenging missions to explore more of the Moon and establish aMoon Baseon the lunar surface for long-term exploration. These missions will set the stage for sending the first astronauts — A

item.title: 特朗普总统签署行政命令创建美国太空学院
item.description:
为了加强国家太空劳动力并培养下一代太空领导人，唐纳德·J·特朗普总统于周五签署了一项行政命令，建立美国第一所美国太空学院。
该命令强调了太空是美国国家安全、经济增长、科学发现和技术创新的关键领域。拟议的学院将重点关注技术教育、领导力发展、纪律和对公共服务的承诺，最终帮助促进美国在太空的利益。
特朗普总统表示：“鉴于美国太空军和商业航天工业的快速发展，以及我们向月球和月球以外地区扩张的野心，很明显，我们需要教育和培训整整一代熟练的军人、工程师和民用操作员。” “这就是为什么我将签署一项行政命令，开始创建一所新的国家学院，名为美国太空学院。”
该命令还要求美国宇航局局长贾里德·艾萨克曼担任美国太空学院新总统委员会的主席，美国宇航局副局长马特·安德森担任执行主任。他们将与副主席——总统科学技术助理迈克尔·克拉齐奥斯(Michael Kratsios)和总统经济政策助理凯文·哈塞特(Kevin Hassett)——以及来自白宫和委员会跨机构的其他代表合作。
艾萨克曼表示：“特朗普总统对新学院的愿景是一个变革性的一步，旨在教育工程师、科学家、技术人员、操作员甚至宇航员，他们对于我们在太空中追求的鼓舞人心的未来至关重要。在未来的几年里，我们将让美国宇航局宇航员重返月球表面，建造月球基地，启动核电，点燃轨道经济，并启动更多的科学和发现任务。” “我毫不怀疑，许多即将毕业并为这些令人兴奋的事业做出贡献的未来人才将在美国太空学院接受教育。”
该委员会应在签署后 120 天内向总统提交一份报告，其中包括有关治理框架、毕业生服务义务、学院的实际位置、立法要求等的建议。
“建立美国太空学院行政命令”的签署仪式在休斯敦的美国宇航局约翰逊航天中心举行，总统还向阿耳忒弥斯二号机组成员颁发了国会太空荣誉勋章。
该行政命令是特朗普总统发布的最新命令，表明他致力于维持美国在太空领域的领导地位，并推进美国宇航局黄金时代的探索和创新。 2025 年 12 月，他签署了《确保美国太空优势》，最近又于 8 月 20 日签署了新的国家太空运输政策备忘录。
在白宫网站上阅读完整的行政命令：
https://www.whitehouse.gov/presidential-actions/2026/08/etting-the-united-states-space-academy

item.title: APOD：2026 年 8 月 28 日 – 天空转向帕拉纳尔之上
item.description:
探索宇宙！每天都会展示我们迷人的宇宙的不同图像或照片，以及由专业天文学家撰写的简短说明。
说明：在欧洲南方天文台位于智利的帕拉纳尔天文台的纬度上，大约以南 25 度，地球的自转使地球表面以每小时超过 1,500 公里的速度向东移动。虽然这比海平面的声速还要快，但这种运动是难以察觉的。尽管如此，通过拍摄星星轨迹，可以在夜空的明显旋转中揭示这种运动。这张星迹图像由 300 个连续 25 秒曝光的数字堆栈组成，这些照片是用固定在三脚架上的相机拍摄的，用于追踪星迹弧线。优美的弧线是同心的，以南天极为中心，南天极是地球自转轴在南半球向太空的延伸。天文台正在运行的一台 1.8 米辅助望远镜 AT 3 出现在南天极下方，在这颗旋转行星精心策划的场景的前景中，微弱地照亮了它。APOD 的 NASA 主要站点正在移动：Fromapod.nasa.govtoscience.nasa.gov/apod明天的图片：太空中的像素

item.title: 康加里国家公园的森林漫滩
item.description:
蜿蜒的康加里河维持着高耸的森林生态系统，并在穿越漫滩时形成了牛弓湖。
在美国 63 个国家公园中，很少有国家公园像南卡罗来纳州的康加里国家公园那样由一条河流的洪泛区来定义。虽然这些特征在其他公园中也很突出，但康加里国家公园 80% 的面积都位于康加里河漫滩内。
这里拥有美国最大的原始底层硬木森林之一。在这张由陆地卫星 9 号上的 OLI（操作陆地成像仪）拍摄的图像中，河流蜿蜒穿过森林覆盖的平原，沿着河流逐渐迁移穿过它时留下的古老河道、山脊和洼地的弯曲绿色带。这些古河道和其他地貌的海拔细微差异会影响它们洪水泛滥的频率，从而产生呈现出对比鲜明的绿色色调的独特生态系统。
河流流经平坦、松软的地形，这有利于形成弯曲和曲流。水通常在弯道外侧流动得更快，当河道切入外河岸时，会导致更快的侵蚀。它在弯曲内侧移动得更慢，导致沉积物沉积和称为点坝的沙质特征的生长。随着时间的推移，这一过程会切断主河道的一个弯道，形成U形牛轭湖。
国家公园管理局将距离游客中心 1.2 英里（1.9 公里）的韦斯顿湖 (Weston Lake) 列为公园内最永久的牛弓湖之一，并指出该湖相对较深，且不像公园内大多数其他牛弓湖（例如魔鬼肘湖）那样具有浅粘土和淤泥层。图像右侧是贝茨老河 (Bates Old River)，这是康加里河 (Congaree River) 的一条大约 4 英里长的废弃河道，还有一个南卡罗来纳州最长的牛轭湖。随着时间的推移，废弃的河道和牛轭湖会充满沉积物，变成浅湿地。其中一些地势低洼、充满水的地貌被称为沼泽，那里往往生长着耐洪的柏树-图珀洛森林。
虽然伐木者在 1880 年代以康加里河沿岸的森林为目标，但频繁的洪水、泥泞的道路和蚊虫肆虐的环境等挑战意味着，大部分洪泛区森林都躲过了大范围的砍伐，而这种砍伐改变了东南部其他地区的情况。到 20 世纪 50 年代，自然资源保护主义者开始认识到该地区这种类型的原始森林已变得多么稀有。国会于 1976 年将该地区指定为国家纪念碑，并于 2003 年成为国家公园。
由于河流蜿蜒穿过公园大部分平坦的地形，因此每年都会多次溢出河岸，通常是在冬季和早春，但也会在飓风和大暴雨过后的夏季和秋季发生。这些洪水在整个洪泛区散布了大片营养丰富的淤泥，滋养了森林，并导致公园内异常高大的树木高度集中。
几十年来，康加里国家公园拥有一系列引人注目的巨型“冠军”树木，这些树木保持着国家和州大小记录。尽管个别树木因受损、死亡或被其他地方新测量的树木超越而获得或失去了冠军地位，但康格瑞树木，如负鼠 (Ilex decidua)、水山核桃 (Carya Aquatica)、火炬松 (Pinus taeda)、月桂栎 (Quercus laurifolia)、沼泽图珀洛 (Nyssa biflora) 和枫香 (Liquidambar) styraciflua）曾多次保持记录。

item.title: 美国宇航局邀请媒体参加土耳其阿耳忒弥斯协议签署仪式
item.description:
土耳其将在下午 2:30 举行的仪式上签署《阿耳忒弥斯协议》。美国东部时间 8 月 31 日星期一，在华盛顿 NASA 总部举行，成为第 71 个签署国。
美国宇航局局长贾里德·艾萨克曼将接待土耳其工业和技术部长穆罕默德·法提赫·卡西尔以及美国国务院官员，出席仪式。
此活动仅限本人参加。有兴趣参加的媒体必须在 8 月 31 日上午 11 点之前回复：hq-media@mail.nasa.gov。 NASA 的媒体认证政策已上线。
2020年，在特朗普第一届政府执政期间，美国在美国宇航局和国务院的领导下，与其他七个创始国共同制定了《阿耳忒弥斯协议》，以回应政府和私营公司对月球活动日益增长的兴趣。
《阿尔忒弥斯协议》引入了第一套实用原则，旨在提高月球、火星及其他地区民用太空探索的安全性、透明度和协调性。

item.title: 关于 NASA 南希·格雷斯·罗马太空望远镜需要了解的 9 件事
item.description:
NASA’s Nancy Grace Roman Space Telescope is set to launch at 7:26 a.m. EDT on Sunday, Aug. 30. While you wait towatch the launch, brush up on some key facts about this wide-view mission.
Roman is named afterDr. Nancy Grace Roman(1925–2018), NASA’s first chief of astronomy. She championed space-based observatories that could study the universe above Earth’s hazy atmosphere while making their data broadly available to the scientific community.While she’s known as the “mother” of the Hubble Space Telescope, Roman played an even broader role as the driving force behind NASA’s entire Great Observatories program, which included Hubble along with the Chandra X-ray Observatory and the retired Compton Gamma Ray Observatory and Spitzer Space Telescope.Her vision and leadership helped establish NASA as a world-class scientific institution and laid the foundation for generations of space telescopes that continue to expand humanity’s understanding of the cosmos.
Roman will pair a large field of view with crisp infrared vision to scan vast, deep swaths of sky. This flagship mission is designed to help astronomers exploredark matter,dark energy, and planets outside our solar system, calledexoplanets.Since each of Roman’s surveys will sample such a large volume of the cosmos, the mission will also offer practically limitless opportunities for astronomers to conduct a broad range of additional science. From objects in our outer solar system and exploding stars to growing black holes and galaxies by the billions, very little will be beyond Roman’s reach. Roman’s data will be made public as soon as it’s processed, allowing many teams to analyze it simultaneously.
Roman will orbit 1 million miles away at the second Sun-Earth Lagrange point (L2), the same location as NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope. At L2, gravity from the Sun and Earth works together with an object’s motion around the Sun to hold it roughly in place. This balance will give Roman a relatively steady orbit without using much fuel.Like Webb, Roman will trace out a large orbit around the actual L2 point — much larger than the Moon’s orbit around Earth — and the two will easily be kept far apart.
This summer, everyone was invited to submit their name to be added to a memory card attached to a plaque on the Roman spacecraft. More than 1.3 million people did so and will have their names carried all the way to L2.
Roman will have a primary mission lifetime of five years and is designed to support an additional five-year extended mission. Fuel is expected to be the mission’s life-limiting resource, and while NASA does not currently have an ability to service observatories at L2, Roman is designed to be refuelable.
The observatory’s Wide Field Instrument is a 300-megapixel infrared camera that will give Roman the same sharpness (angular resolution) as Hubble but with a field of view at least 100 times larger. Using this instrument, each Roman image will capture a patch of the sky about 1.5 times bigger than the apparent size of a full Moon.Roman’s Coronagraph Instrument is designed to demonstrate the most advanced technologies ever flown in space for directly imaging planets around other stars. It will block the glare from stars and make it possible for scientists to see the faint reflected light from planets in orbit around them, revealing giant worlds that are older, colder, and in closer orbits than the hot, young super-Jupiters direct imaging has mainly revealed so far.
Roman will work in tandem with many other NASA-led and international missions to provide the most complete view of our universe yet. Roman’s large panoramas will uncover interesting targets that Hubble could follow up on using infrared, visible, and ultraviolet light to offer a more comprehensive view. NASA’s James Webb Space Telescope can then use its larger mirror and more powerful vision to deliver even more detailed, ultra-sharp observations. And Roman can view regions around objects Hubble or Webb observe to offer context.Euclid, an ESA (European Space Agency) mission with key contributions from NASA, will observe a larger area of the sky than Roman, though with less detail. Since their survey areas will overlap, scientists can use Roman’s higher-quality data to apply corrections to Euclid’s, then extend these refinements over Euclid’s much larger area.Scientists can also pair Roman’s infrared data with visible-light observations from the ground-based Vera C. Rubin Observatory, a National Science Foundation–Department of Energy collaboration. That will allow astronomers to inch closer to achieving Roman-like quality over Rubin’s much greater sky coverage.By showcasing technology to directly photograph Jupiter-like exoplanets, Roman will also provide a crucial stepping stone for NASA’sHabitable Worlds Observatoryconcept, a flagship space telescope that would be designed to photograph Earth-like planets in other solar systems for the first time ever.
